question: Under the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act 2021 in India, which of the following statements about gamete donation is correct?

answers.text: Commercial gamete donation (payment to donors) is permitted under the Act

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Commercial gamete donation is prohibited under the ART Act 2021. Only altruistic donation with reimbursement of direct expenses is permitted. Paid gamete donation is a criminal offence under the Act.

answers.text: A woman may donate oocytes to more than five couples in her lifetime under the Act

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The ART Act 2021 restricts a woman to donating oocytes to a maximum of one couple and only once in her lifetime — this protects against ovarian hyperstimulation risk from multiple donation cycles.

answers.text: Gamete donation is restricted to altruistic donation, and a single woman may only donate oocytes once in her lifetime

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The ART (Regulation) Act 2021 bans commercial gamete donation, allows only altruistic donation, and restricts oocyte donation to once per woman per lifetime — safeguarding donor health and preventing exploitation.

answers.text: Sperm donation from anonymous donors is banned; the recipient couple must know the donor identity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The ART Act 2021 permits anonymous sperm donation. Anonymity provisions are actually maintained in the legislation to protect donor privacy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Under the ART (Regulation) Act 2021, commercial donation is prohibited; only altruistic donation is allowed. A woman may donate oocytes only once in her lifetime to one couple.
Well done. The ART Act 2021 mandates altruistic (non-commercial) donation and limits oocyte donation to once per woman — these are directly examinable facts.
